This provides a buffer for systems updates before the screen rate goes dark.

[ERROR NAME]: Fragmented Settlement Risk (Orphaned Senior Funding) [What NOT to do]: Do not permit Senior Lenders to settle funds into the Transaction Account without a mechanism to verify that Subordinated/Mezzanine Lenders have also funded their respective shares on the same day. [Why it's wrong]: If Senior Lenders fund but Junior Lenders fail to settle (e.g., due to operational error or liquidity issues), the Senior debt is deployed without the required credit enhancement (First Loss protection). The Issuer holds Senior cash without the corresponding Junior equity cushion. [What TO do]: Include a 'Return of Funds' clause (see Clause 6.5) stating that if the Subordinated/Mezzanine amounts are not credited by a specific cutoff time (e.g., 5:00 p.m.), the Senior Advance must be returned immediately to the Senior Lender. Make the Senior Lenders' obligation to fund conditional upon the simultaneous funding of the Junior tranches.

[ERROR NAME]: Transfer Cost Leakage (Missing Historical Cap) [What NOT to do]: When drafting assignment/transfer clauses, do not grant New Lenders the full benefit of Tax Gross-Up or Increased Cost indemnities without limitation. [Why it's wrong]: If an Existing Lender transfers to a New Lender located in a jurisdiction with higher tax requirements or regulatory costs, the Issuer's liabilities increase solely due to the Lender's choice. This can degrade the SPV's cash flow. [What TO do]: Include a 'Historical Cap' (see Clause 18.3.1), stating that a New Lender is only entitled to receive payments under Increased Costs or Tax Indemnity clauses to the *same extent* that the Existing Lender would have been entitled had the transfer not occurred. Exception: Only lift this cap if the assignment occurs during an Event of Default.

[ERROR NAME]: Pre-Funding Negative Carry [What NOT to do]: When allowing 'Pre-Funding' (borrowing Senior Advances based on *expected* rather than *actual* origination), do not allow the Issuer to hold that cash indefinitely if the receivables are not acquired. [Why it's wrong]: Borrowing money costs the Senior Interest Rate (e.g., SONIA + Margin). Cash sitting in a Transaction Account earns a lower Deposit Rate. Holding unused Pre-Funding creates 'Negative Carry' (economic loss) for the SPV. [What TO do]: Implement a mandatory 'Pre-Funding Sweep' (see Clause 6.6). Any amount standing to the credit of the Pre-Funding Ledger that has not been used to purchase receivables by the next Monthly Payment Date must be repaid to the Senior Lenders. Do not allow it to roll over into subsequent periods.

[ERROR NAME]: Solvency Certificate Jurisdictional Defect [What NOT to do]: When drafting Solvency Certificates for Issuers with assets or incorporation outside England & Wales, do not rely solely on citations of the Insolvency Act 1986 (e.g., s123, s238). [Why it's wrong]: Specific insolvency concepts like 'Gratuitous Alienation' (Scotland) or specific NI Orders differ from English law. A certificate citing only English statutes may be defective in proving solvency in a Scottish or Northern Irish court. [What TO do]: Explicitly cite the jurisdictional equivalents in the Solvency Certificate. For Scotland, cite Section 242 of the Insolvency Act 1986 (Gratuitous Alienation) and common law equivalents. For Northern Ireland, cite Article 102 of the Insolvency (Northern Ireland) Order 1989. (See Schedule 5, Clause 5.2.3 and 5.2.9).

[ERROR NAME]: Asymmetric Make-Whole Calculation: Do NOT use a static calculation period (e.g., '36 months from Closing') for all voluntary cancellation fee scenarios. You must conditionally reduce the make-whole period (e.g., to '24 months' or similar shortened duration) if the cancellation results from the Original Senior Lender's own refusal to extend or exercise of a termination option (as seen in Clause 8.1.1.4). Applying the full make-whole duration when the lender itself forces the exit is contradictory and commercially punitive.

[ERROR NAME]: Restrictive Assignment Triggers: When restricting Lender assignments (requiring Seller consent), do NOT limit the 'Free Transfer' exceptions solely to Events of Default. You must also include 'Perfection Events' (as in Clause 18.3.1(c)), even if the Revolving Period has ended. A Perfection Event indicates credit deterioration of the Originator (triggering legal title transfer), which validates the Lender's need to freely transfer risk even if a hard Event of Default has not yet occurred.

[ERROR NAME]: Issuer Illegality Substitution Omission: In 'Illegality of Issuer' clauses, do NOT mandate immediate repayment as the sole remedy. You must include a mandatory mitigation mechanism requiring the Issuer to procure its substitution with another SPV (subject to Lender approval) if this cures the illegality (as in Clause 7.10). Unlike corporate loans, securitization structures are costly to unwind; substitution preserves the asset-backed structure against regulatory changes affecting only the specific SPV entity.

[ERROR NAME]: Stranded Capacity (Drawdown Minimum): When setting minimum utilisation amounts (e.g., 'Minimum £1,000,000'), always include the proviso 'or, if less, the Senior Available Commitments' (as in Clause 6.7.2). Omitting this tail creates a 'Stranded Capacity' issue where the final portion of the facility (e.g., a remaining £500k) becomes undrawable because it falls below the minimum threshold.

definitions.content: Account Bank Eligible Institution: means any Issuer Account Bank, Collections Account Bank or any proposed Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank, as at any date of determination, that: (a) is and remains duly authorised in respect of its deposit taking activities under the laws of the jurisdiction in which it is operating; and (b) if it is not an Electronic Money Institution, maintains certain corporate ratings, which are short term unsecured, unguaranteed and unsubordinated debt obligations rated at least P-1 by Moody’s, A-l by S&P and F-1 by Fitch; or (c) if it is an Electronic Money Institution, is an Approved Electronic Money Institution.

Account Bank Event: means, in respect of an Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank, any of: (a) the occurrence of an Insolvency Event; (b) it being or becoming subject to Insolvency Proceedings; (c) to the extent such Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank is an Electronic Money Institution, an “insolvency event” occurs with respect to it or it becomes subject to “insolvency proceedings”, each as defined in the Electronic Money Regulations 2011/99; (d) to the extent that such Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank is an Electronic Money Institution as at the date on which it is appointed to act as an Account Bank for the purposes of this Transaction, on any subsequent date it is no longer registered or authorised as an Electronic Money Institution; (e) the occurrence of an Account Bank Downgrade; or (f) any event of default (or equivalent event) or breach by the Issuer Account Bank or Collections Account Bank, as the case may be, is continuing in respect of the relevant account bank under the Issuer Account Bank Agreement or any Acknowledgment of Collections Account Declaration of Trust executed by the account bank.

Adjusted Loan Terms: means, in respect of any Receivable and its related Consumer Loan, that it has been originated in circumstances in which the Borrower had originally specified an amount of borrowing and term of the loan at the time the Borrower applied for the Consumer Loan and the Seller subsequently offered to that Borrower an option to adjust the loan terms by increasing or decreasing the amount of borrowing and/or the term of the proposed Consumer Loan and the Borrower consequently adjusted the terms of their initial application.

Agreed Adjusted Ad Hoc Funding Amount: means, as at any Cut-Off Date, an amount equal to the higher of: (a) zero; and (b) an amount equal to: (i) the aggregate Agreed Ad Hoc Funding Amounts incurred from and including the Closing Date up to and including that Cut-Off Date; and (ii) the aggregate of the amounts calculated under paragraph (ii)(A)(2)(cc) of the definition of Subordinated Redemption Amount, from and including the Closing Date up to and including that Cut-Off Date.

Available Distribution Amount: means, as at the applicable Cut-Off Date that relates to a Borrowing Base Report, an amount equal to: (a) for the purposes of determining funds that may be applied towards Initial Purchase Price on any Purchase Date other than a Monthly Payment Date or the payment of Subordinated Settlement Repayment Amount on any Weekly Utilisation Date, the amount (without double counting) equal to the sum of the amount standing to the credit of: (i) prior to the Issuer Collections Account Effective Date, the Transaction Account and the Pre-Funding Account; and (ii) from (and including) the Issuer Collections Account Effective Date: (A) the Issuer Collections Account and the Pre-Funding Account; and (B) any amounts requested by the Issuer under a Senior Utilisation Request or Mezzanine Funding Request pursuant to the terms of any Facility Agreement which will be credited to the Transaction Account: provided, in each case, that it shall not include any amounts advanced to the Issuer for the purposes of crediting the Pre-Funding Account or Cash Reserve Account; (1) in respect of the payment of the Subordinated Settlement Repayment Amount on a Weekly Utilisation Date, on the relevant Weekly Utilisation Date; (2) in respect of the payment of Initial Purchase Price on a Purchase Date, on the relevant Purchase Date, (b) for the purposes of calculating the available funds to be applied on any Monthly Payment Date in accordance with the applicable Priority of Payments, the amount (without double counting) equal to the sum of: (i) the sum of all amounts standing to the credit of the Transaction Account (other than amounts standing to the credit of the Issuer Profit Ledger), Issuer Collections Account and the Cash Reserve Account including, following the occurrence of a Security Enforcement Event, any other proceeds from the enforcement of security over the Purchased Receivables; (ii) any amounts requested by the Issuer under a Senior Utilisation Request, Mezzanine Funding Request pursuant to the terms of any Facility Agreement which will stand to the credit of the Transaction Account for the purpose of financing the acquisition of Receivables on any Monthly Payment Date in accordance with the Priority of Payments, provided that it shall not include any amounts advanced to the Issuer for the purposes of crediting the Pre-Funding Account or Cash Reserve Account; (iii) on any Monthly Payment Date, any amount to be received by the Issuer from a Swap Provider in accordance with any Swap Agreement, other than amounts described in paragraph (iv) below; (iv) any amount to be received by the Issuer from a Swap Provider in accordance with any Swap Agreement which is a Swap Termination Amount which is not required to be applied to purchase a replacement swap transaction and any amount described in clause 15.2 (Premium Received by the Issuer) or clause 15.3 (Termination payment received by the Issuer) of the Cash Management Agreement; plus (v) in respect of any Monthly Payment Date occurring during the period from the Closing Date to the date that is six months after the Closing Date, amounts advanced under the Subordinated Facility to be applied pursuant to any of items 1 to 19 of the Pre-Enforcement Priority of Payments, and at any other time, amounts requested by the Issuer (or the Servicer acting on its behalf) under a Subordinated Utilisation Request pursuant to the terms of the Subordinated Facility Agreement which will stand to the credit of the Transaction Account.

Cash Reserve Target Amount: means, as at any date of determination, an amount equal to: (a) as at any date occurring prior to the end of the Revolving Period, 0.75 per cent of the aggregate Senior Principal Amount Outstanding as at that date (after taking account of any increase or decrease of the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding that day); and (b) as at any date occurring after the end of the Revolving Period, zero.

Concentration Limits: means the concentration limits set out in Part A (Applicable Concentration Limits) Schedule 3 (Concentration Limits) to the Master Framework Agreement, as amended from time to time, including pursuant to Clause 3.33 (Amendment of Eligibility Criteria or Concentration Limits) of the Master Framework Agreement. [Note: Content of Schedule 3 extracted for completeness]: (a) Average Weighted Remaining Term: the aggregate weighted average remaining term of the Purchased Receivables as at the date of determination may not exceed 50 months; (b) Minimum Weighted Average APR: the Weighted Average APR as at the date of determination is greater than the sum of the aggregate weighted average Swap Rate in respect of the Senior Advances and a margin equal to 9.5 per cent.; (c) Single Employer: if the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables is: (i) less than GBP 100,000,000, the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables that are outstanding originated through a single Employer Partner is not greater than 25.0 per cent. of the aggregate portfolio; (ii) greater than or equal to GBP 100,000,000, the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables that are outstanding originated through a single employer partner is not greater than 20.0 per cent. of the aggregate portfolio; (d) Top Five Employer Partner: the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables that are outstanding from the Borrowers that are Employees of an Employer Partner in a Top Five Employer Partner is not greater than 50.0 per cent. of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables; (e) Direct Debit/Push Payments: the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables that are outstanding and granted to Borrowers that are paying through direct debit or Push Payment for at least two consecutive calendar months (instead of by way of Salary Deduction) is not greater than 19.0 per cent. of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables; (f) Push Payments only: the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables that are outstanding and granted to Borrowers that are paying through Push Payment for at least two consecutive calendar months (instead of by way of Salary Deduction or direct debit) is not greater than 3.5 per cent. of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables; (g) Adjusted Loan Terms Prime Borrowers only: the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables which have been subject to/originated as a result of Adjusted Loan Terms advanced to Borrowers that have been classified as Prime Borrowers in accordance with the Seller’s underwriting policies and where the amended monthly payment is greater than the original monthly payment is not greater than 12.0 per cent. of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables; (h) Adjusted Loan Term Near Prime Borrowers only: the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables which have been subject to/originated as a result of Adjusted Loan Terms advanced to Borrowers that have been classified as Near Prime Borrowers in accordance with the Seller’s underwriting policies and where the amended monthly payment is greater than the original monthly payment is not greater than 4.0 per cent. of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables; and (i) Subprime Borrowers: the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables that are outstanding and granted to Subprime Borrowers is not greater than 20.0 per cent. of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables; (j) Subprime Borrowers/Near Prime Borrowers (Senior): the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables that are outstanding and granted to Subprime Borrowers and Near Prime Borrowers is not greater than 60.0 per cent. of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables.

Coverage Requirement: means the requirement that: (a) each of the Swap Agreements entered into by the Issuer (as applicable) is in full force and effect and has not been terminated; and (b) the Swap Agreements entered into by the Issuer and the related Hedge Transactions have a notional that covers at least 90 per cent. and no more than 110 per cent. of the total Senior Principal Amount Outstanding on a Hedging Test Date.

Cut-Off Date: means: (a) in respect of any Borrowing Base Report, 11.59 pm on either the day prior, or two days prior, to the Borrowing Base Reporting Date, on which the relevant Borrowing Base Report is to be delivered; or (b) in respect of any Monthly Servicer Report, all information available to the Servicer for the purposes of reporting at 11:59 pm on the day, or two days, immediately preceding the Monthly Servicer Report Date on which the Monthly Servicer Report is to be delivered.

Default Rate: means, on any Determination Date, in respect of the Collection Period ending on that date, the rate (expressed as a percentage) equal to the quotient of: (a) the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that have become Defaulted Receivables during that Collection Period; and (b) the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that are not Defaulted Receivables, as of the end of the fourth Collection Period preceding that Collection Period.

Delinquency Rate: means, on any Determination Date, in respect of the Collection Period ending on that date, the rate (expressed as a percentage) equal to the quotient of: (a) the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that are Delinquent Receivables; and (b) the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables that are not Defaulted Receivables, as of the end of the third Collection Period preceding that Collection Period.

Delinquent Receivable: means, in respect of any Receivable, it remains unpaid past its due date for a period equal to, or more than, 31 days but less than 90 days, provided that: (a) any Receivable that remains unpaid past its due date for a period equal to, or more than, 31 days solely as a consequence of a systems failure or other technical failure that prevents the affected Employer Partner from making the relevant payment and/or [PARTY_NAME] from reconciling the funds received by it from an Employer Partner (provided that, once the Employer Partner has resolved the systems failure or other technical failure or has otherwise sent the relevant information to [PARTY_NAME], [PARTY_NAME] has not failed to reconcile such funds within two Business Days of such resolution or receipt of information) shall, subject to paragraph (b) below, not constitute a Delinquent Receivable; and (b) the systems failure or other technical failure referred to in sub-paragraph (a) above must be remedied within a period of 31 days of the Servicer becoming aware of such failure or being notified of the same by the Employer Partner.

Eligible Receivable: means, as at any date of determination, any Purchased Receivable satisfying the criteria set out at ‎Schedule 2 (Eligibility Criteria) to the Master Framework Agreement. [Note: Content of Schedule 2 extracted for completeness]: (a) Ordinary course of business: has been advanced to an Employee of an Employer Partner of the Seller and originated and underwritten by the Seller in the ordinary course of its business; (b) Not a Defaulted or Delinquent Receivable: is not a Defaulted Receivable or Delinquent Receivable; (c) Purchased Receivables Representations and Warranties: as at the Purchase Date, there has been no breach of any of the representations and warranties relating to that Purchased Receivable set out in Part C of Schedule 7; (d) No modification or restructuring: has not been subject to any restructuring or modification, other than a Permitted Modification, at any time; (e) Fully disbursed: is fully disbursed with no possible or potential future funding obligations (other than any Further Advance expressly permitted in accordance with the terms of the applicable Borrower Agreement); (f) Payment term: has an original term to maturity from the date of the first advance which is less than or equal to 60 months and greater than or equal to six months; (g) Remaining term: at the time of origination, had a remaining term of at least one month; (h) Maximum initial principal balance: has an initial Outstanding Principal Balance of no greater than GBP 25,000; (i) Minimum initial principal balance: has an initial Outstanding Principal Balance of no less than GBP 250; (j) Maximum instalment to net income ratio: the loan instalments payable under the terms of the Receivable did not exceed 52.0 per cent. of the Borrower’s net monthly income at the time of application; (k) No amount outstanding: as at its Purchase Date only, had no amount due and payable in connection with it by the Borrower which remained unpaid past its due date; (l) No payment holiday: was not the subject of a payment holiday at that time; (m) Payment Method: as at the date when it is acquired by the Issuer, is only payable by way of Salary Deduction; or otherwise via direct debit or Push Payment only if the relevant Borrower is an Employee of an Employer Partner which does not have Salary Deduction arrangements; (n) Payable to the Collections Account: will be, and any Collections in relation to it will be, credited directly to a Collections Account; (o) Currency: is denominated and payable in GBP; (p) Interest rate: has a fixed rate of interest of at least 3.9 per cent. per annum but no more than 34.9 per cent per annum; (q) Unsecured: is unsecured; (r) Transfer and Validity of Sale: [Standard valid sale criteria]; (s) No revocation, set-off or counter-claim: is not the subject of any right of revocation, set-off or counter-claim; (t) No litigation: is not the subject of any litigation; (u) Originated and administered in accordance with Applicable Law: [Standard compliance]; (v) Originated and administered in accordance with Seller Documentation and Policies: [Standard compliance]; (w) No fraud or illegal activity: [Standard]; (x) Identification of Receivable: [Standard]; (y) No Tax: [Standard]; (z) No bill of exchange or promissory note: [Standard]; (aa) Top-Up Receivable: if it is a Top-Up Receivable, it has been originated and administered in accordance with all Seller Documentation and Policies relevant to Top-Up Receivables.

Employer Partner Event: means, with respect to any Employer Partner, the occurrence of any of the following: (a) the commencement of any collective redundancy consultation process pursuant to Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992; or (b) any Insolvency Event or Insolvency Proceedings being threatened or commenced against it.
Final Maturity Date: means the first Monthly Payment Date falling 60 months after the end of the Revolving Period.

Issuer Profit Amount: means GBP 1,200 per annum, credited in equal portions on each Monthly Payment Date to the Issuer Profit Ledger and to be retained (subject to the payment by the Issuer therefrom of any corporation tax due from the Issuer in respect of its profits) by the Issuer as profit in respect of the business of the Issuer.

Mezzanine Advance Rate: means, as at any date of determination, the weighted average percentage that is calculated by applying the following, as relevant: (a) 95 per cent. for the Outstanding Principal Balance of all Eligible Receivables, excluding any Receivables falling within the Subprime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount; and (b) 70.5 per cent. for the Subprime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount, in each case, as at that date.

Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event: means, as at any Determination Date, any of the following events: (a) the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of Purchased Receivables that are outstanding in respect of Borrowers that are paying by way of direct debit or Push Payments for at least two consecutive calendar months ending on that Determination Date (rather than by way of Salary Deduction), excluding for the purposes of this calculation any Purchased Receivables that have been delinquent for more than 90 days, is greater than 19.0 per cent. of the aggregate Outstanding Principal Balance of all Purchased Receivables, excluding for the purposes of this calculation any Purchased Receivables that have been outstanding for more than 90 days; (b) the Default Rate across the most recent consecutive three-month period is greater than 1.25 per cent., as calculated on each relevant Determination Date; or (c) the Default Rate across the most recent consecutive three-month period is greater than 0.75 per cent., as calculated on each relevant Determination Date, provided that, following the occurrence of (a) and/or (b) and/or (c), where the relevant breach, or breaches, has, or have, been remedied and no further breach has occurred for at least three consecutive Determination Dates, no reduction to the Mezzanine Advance Rate shall apply (and no waiver in this respect shall be required).

Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Percentage: means: (a) 5.0 per cent., which shall be applicable if a Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing that relates to paragraphs (a) or (b) of the definition of Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event; or (b) 2.5 per cent, which shall be applicable if a Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing that relates to paragraph (c) of the definition of Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event and no Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing that relates to paragraphs (a) or (b) of the definition of Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event.

Mezzanine Borrowing Base: means: (a) on any Monthly Payment Date, any Funding Request Date, any Funding Date and any Purchase Date when no Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing, without double-counting or double-deductions, an amount equal to: (i) the product of: (A) the Mezzanine Advance Rate as at the immediately preceding Cut-Off Date; and (B) the Mezzanine Net Eligible Receivables Balance as at the immediately preceding Cut-Off Date; plus (ii) the sum of: (A) the balance standing to the credit of the Transaction Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Transaction Account on that date); (B) the balance standing to the credit of the Issuer Collections Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Issuer Collections Account on that date); and (C) the balance standing to the credit of the Pre-Funding Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Pre-Funding Account on that date); less (iii) the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding as at that date; or (b) on any Monthly Payment Date, any Funding Request Date, any Funding Date and any Purchase Date when a Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event is continuing, without double-counting or double-deductions, an amount equal to: (i) the product of: (A) the Mezzanine Advance Rate as at the Cut-Off Date immediately preceding the occurrence of the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event that is continuing; and (B) the Mezzanine Net Eligible Receivables Balance that relates to each Purchased Receivable that has a Purchase Date prior to the Cut-Off Date immediately preceding the occurrence of the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event that is continuing; plus (ii) the product of: (A) the percentage that is equal to: (1) the Mezzanine Advance Rate; less (2) the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Percentage; and (B) the Mezzanine Net Eligible Receivables Balance that relates to each Purchased Receivable that has a Purchase Date on or following the Cut-Off Date immediately preceding the occurrence of the Mezzanine Advance Rate Reduction Event that is continuing; plus (iii) the sum of: (A) the balance standing to the credit of the Transaction Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Transaction Account on that date); (B) the balance standing to the credit of the Issuer Collections Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Issuer Collections Account on that date); and (C) the balance standing to the credit of the Pre-Funding Account (after taking into account any amounts credited to or debited from the Pre-Funding Account on that date); less (iv) the Senior Principal Amount Outstanding as at that date.

Near Prime Borrower: means a Borrower that, for the purposes of the Seller’s underwriting and completion of a responsible lending assessment in respect of that Borrower, has obtained: (a) a Gauge 2 Score of at least 551 and no more than 590; and (b) a Delphi 11SBN Score of at least 611 and no more than 790.

Perfection Event: means the occurrence of any Early Amortisation Event, other than events relating to: (a) Performance Ratios or Triggers; (b) Payments not made by Salary Deduction; (c) the Senior Borrowing Base; (d) the Cash Reserve being less than the Cash Reserve Target Amount on any Monthly Payment Date solely due to insufficient Available Distribution Amount (rather than failure to fund via Subordinated Advance); (e) Excess Spread triggers (applicable after six months from the Closing Date); (f) Change of Control; or (g) Issuer Account Bank Events.

Prime Borrower: means a Borrower that, where used for the purposes of underwriting and responsible lending assessment, has obtained: (a) a Gauge 2 Score of at least 591; and (b) a Delphi 11SBN Score of at least 791.

Senior Advance Rate: means, as at any date of determination, the percentage equal to: (a) the weighted average percentage that is calculated by applying the following, as relevant: (i) 84.50 per cent. for the Outstanding Principal Balance of all Eligible Receivables, excluding any Receivables falling within the Subprime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount or Near Prime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount; (ii) 60.00 per cent. for the Subprime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount; and (iii) 77.50 per cent. for the Near Prime Reduced Advance Rate Concentration Amount, in each case, as at that date; or (b) any other percentage agreed in writing between the Senior Lenders and the Seller from time to time.
Senior Advance Rate Reduction Percentage: means 5.00 per cent.

Subordinated Settlement Date: means any date on which the Issuer redeems the Subordinated Loan, in part, by an amount equal to the aggregate Initial Purchase Price paid by the Issuer since the immediately preceding Subordinated Settlement Date or Monthly Payment Date, whichever occurred most recently, solely by way of advances under the Subordinated Loan.
Subprime Advance Rate Reduction Limit: means an amount equal to 8.0 per cent of the Senior Net Eligible Receivables Balance.

Subprime Borrower: means a Borrower that, for the purposes of the Seller’s underwriting and completion of a responsible lending assessment in respect of that Borrower, has obtained: (a) a Gauge 2 Score of no more than 550; and (b) a Delphi 11SBN Score of no more than 610.
Transaction Default Rate: means: (a) the Senior Interest Rate; or (b) the Mezzanine Note Interest Rate, plus 2.00 per cent., in each case.

“Acceding Swap Provider Minimum Rating” means, in relation to a new or successor Swap Provider that is not an affiliate of Swap Provider, a rating for its long-term unsecured and non-credit-enhanced debt obligations of A or higher by S&P or Fitch or A2 or higher by Moody’s.

Incremental Mezzanine Facility Amount: means the principal amount of any additional mezzanine notes or advances that may be issued or borrowed under the Mezzanine Facility Agreement in accordance with accordion or incremental facility provisions, subject to the satisfaction of specified conditions.

Northern Irish Receivable Recharacterisation Event: means any judgment, decree, declaration, decision or order (whether interim or final) of any supervisory authority, tribunal, court or other governmental authority that requires any Receivable originated by the Seller or other unsecured personal loan (whether originated by the Originator or any other party) entered into with a borrower or consumer resident in Northern Ireland, to be subject to, or otherwise construed in accordance with, Northern Irish law (in whole or in part) in accordance with overriding mandatory provisions of Northern Irish law, rather than the law which the Receivable or unsecured personal loan is expressed to be governed in accordance with its contractual terms.

“Blocking Law” means (i) Council Regulation (EC) 2271/96 (or any law or regulation implementing such Regulation in any member state of the European Union), (ii) any similar law or regulation in the United Kingdom, or (iii) Section 7 of the German Foreign Trade Regulation (Außenwirtschaftsverordnung).
“Push Payment” means any payment that is: (a) made manually by a Borrower; or (b) made by a third party (other than an Employer Partner) in the context of an IVA or a debt management plan.

Compliance Uplift: means an increase in the applicable margin or interest rate payable on the transaction securities or facility, typically triggered by a failure to deliver required compliance certificates, reporting packages, or other information requirements by the specified deadline.

Enforcement Consultation Period: means a specified period of time following the occurrence of an Event of Default or Termination Event during which the Security Trustee or Noteholder Representative is required to consult with the Transaction Parties or Instructing Creditors regarding potential enforcement actions or the realization of Security before such actions are taken.

“ESG Issue” means a finding by regulatory or law enforcement agencies that a person has materially violated any applicable law or regulation relating to: protection of the environment; worker safety; fair wages and working conditions; collective bargaining; unlawful discrimination; child or forced labour; bribery or corruption; consumer, patient or tenant protection or privacy; fair treatment of customers; product or drug safety; or taxation.

“Majority Senior Lenders” means: (a) while any member of the Original Senior Lender Group is a party to any Transaction Document: (i) on any date during the Revolving Period, each member of the Original Senior Lender Group that is party to any Transaction Document (notwithstanding the proportion of the Senior Total Commitments that their related Senior Commitments comprise); or (ii) from (and including) the Termination Date, a Senior Lender or Senior Lenders whose aggregate Senior Principal Amounts Outstanding on that date aggregate more than 66⅔ per cent. of all Senior Principal Amounts Outstanding on that date, provided that, if any member of the Original Senior Lender Group is a party to any Transaction Document, the consent of that member of the Original Senior Lender Group that is party to any Transaction Document shall also be required; or (b) if no member of the Original Senior Lender Group is a party to any Transaction Document: (i) on any date during the Revolving Period, a Senior Lender or Senior Lenders whose Senior Commitments on that date aggregate more than 66⅔ per cent. of the Senior Total Commitments on that date; or (ii) from (and including) the Termination Date, a Senior Lender or Senior Lenders whose aggregate Senior Principal Amounts Outstanding on that date aggregate more than 66⅔ per cent. of all Senior Principal Amounts Outstanding on that date.
Mezzanine Total Commitments Increase Limit: means the maximum aggregate amount to which the Mezzanine Total Commitments may be increased in accordance with the Transaction Documents.
Minimum Excess Spread Amount: means the minimum required amount of Excess Spread to be retained by the Issuer, often set at a nominal value to satisfy tax, legal, or corporate existence requirements.

“Most Senior Lenders” means: (a) for so long as there is any Senior Commitment outstanding or there is any amount outstanding under the Senior Loans, the Majority Senior Lenders; (b) at any time that paragraph (a) does not apply, and for so long as there is any Mezzanine Commitment outstanding, there is any Mezzanine Note outstanding or the total commitments to provide Mezzanine Facilities under the Mezzanine Facility Agreement are greater than zero, the Mezzanine Note Purchasers; and (c) at any time that paragraph (a) and (b) do not apply, the Subordinated Lender.
ABS Transaction Fee: means any fee payable to any member of the Original Senior Lender Group for its role in an ABS Transaction as sole arranger and joint lead manager.

Rejected Senior Total Commitments Increase Counter Offer: means the event where the Senior Total Commitments Increase Counter Offer is rejected by any of the Issuer, Seller or Servicer and, following discussions between each of the Senior Lenders, Seller, Servicer and the Issuer, no terms for the Senior Total Commitments Increase are agreed, upon which there shall be no increase to the Senior Total Commitments and the Exclusivity Provisions shall cease to apply.
